title: P53CORE is a gene-program score, not a drug label
takeaway: A 32-gene p53/DNA-damage response program was defined in the user's analysis as P53CORE.
explanation: A program score can summarize coordinated expression beyond a single marker gene.
caution: The exact 32-gene composition is an internal user-defined set; it is not independently validated as a unique radiotherapy-exposure biomarker.
question: Which is a valid inference from an elevated P53CORE score?
options: Genes in the chosen p53-associated program are relatively upregulated
Radiotherapy exposure is uniquely identified by the program
TP53 mutation status is directly determined by expression of the program

reference.label: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory, Nature (2026)

decisionRule: Record the actual 32 genes and score definition, then test matched irradiation, untreated and alternative-stress controls. A high score alone identifies a program, not treatment history.

title: The p53 response has multiple possible outcomes
takeaway: p53 regulates responses to DNA damage and stress, including cell-cycle arrest, repair-associated transcription, senescence and sometimes apoptosis.
explanation: Different cell contexts can express different p53-associated gene subsets.
caution: A p53-related score does not diagnose a TP53 mutation or uniquely indicate irradiation.
question: Does p53 activation always mean apoptosis?
options: No; cell-cycle arrest and other outcomes are possible
Yes; every activated cell dies immediately
Yes; only T cells can activate p53

reference.label: GBM state and trajectory literature

decisionRule: Compare CDKN1A/MDM2-associated arrest or feedback targets with pro-apoptotic p53 targets and observed viability; context, TP53 status and treatment affect the response.

title: Radiotherapy uses ionizing radiation
takeaway: Radiotherapy exposes a target region to ionizing radiation to damage cells and control tumor growth.
explanation: Ionizing radiation can induce DNA damage responses across tumor and nonmalignant compartments.
caution: Exposure cannot be reconstructed with certainty from a generic DNA-damage score alone.
question: What makes radiation 'ionizing'?
options: It can remove electrons from atoms or molecules
It is always visible light
It is only a form of ultrasound

reference.label: Stupp et al., NEJM (2005), PMID 15758009

decisionRule: Radiation dose and field are exposure metadata; DNA-damage transcription alone cannot distinguish RT from other genotoxic stresses.

title: Two developmental-like programs in the 2026 GB atlas
takeaway: The 2026 GBM atlas distinguishes NPC–OPC-like and NPC–neuronal-like malignant programs resembling distinct neural developmental states.
explanation: A tumor may contain malignant cells with different neural progenitor-like transcription.
caution: These are transcriptional analogies within a specific atlas, not proof of normal-cell lineage.
question: You detect two genetically malignant GBM clusters. Cluster A: OLIG1, PDGFRA and SOX6-associated program. Cluster B: DCX, STMN2 and SOX11-associated program. Which interpretation is best?
options: A resembles the NPC–OPC-like program; B resembles NPC–neuronal-like transcription
A is necessarily a normal OPC and B is necessarily a normal neuron
The programs prove two independently traced cell lineages

reference.label: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory, Nature (2026)

decisionRule: Compare NPC–OPC-like modules (for example OLIG-family/PDGFRA-associated programs) against NPC–neuronal-like modules (for example STMN2/DCX/SOX11-associated programs), while verifying malignant identity separately.
optionFeedback: Correct: these are comparative malignant transcriptional programs in a specific GBM atlas, not mature-cell identity claims.
Incorrect: independently established malignant cells can express developmental programs without becoming normal progenitors or neurons.
Incorrect: expression classes alone do not constitute lineage tracing.

title: GBM contains many nonmalignant compartments
takeaway: A GBM microenvironment can include microglia, macrophages, T cells, astrocytes, endothelial cells, pericytes and extracellular matrix.
explanation: A spatial tumor atlas can distinguish immune, vascular, neural and malignant regions.
caution: These compartments vary by patient and region; a marker alone may not unambiguously identify a cell type.
question: Which belongs to the tumor microenvironment?
options: Vascular and immune cells
Immune cells and malignant cells, but not vascular or matrix compartments
Immune and vascular cells, but not extracellular matrix or soluble signals

reference.label: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory, Nature (2026)

decisionRule: Inspect cell-type panels: myeloid markers such as LST1; vascular PECAM1/VWF; astrocytic AQP4/GFAP; T-cell CD3D/E. Assignments need co-expression and contamination checks.

title: Both genetics and environment influence malignant state
takeaway: GBM cell states reflect intrinsic genetic programs and extrinsic tissue microenvironment cues.
explanation: Different clones or regions can show differing state frequencies.
caution: Spatial association does not establish an environmentally caused state transition.
question: Which evidence would strengthen a causal niche claim?
options: A controlled perturbation changing the niche while tracking cell states
A spatial ligand–receptor association replicated in multiple untreated tumors
A matching expression gradient within the same tumor without perturbation

reference.label: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory, Nature (2026)

decisionRule: Compare cells of a matched genetic clone across neighborhoods or perturb the niche and measure state changes; a genotype–environment correlation alone is not causal.

title: Heterogeneity does not identify a unique trajectory
takeaway: The same tumor can contain multiple malignant states and may display plasticity.
explanation: Researchers ask which transitions are reproducible and whether states are reversible.
caution: Cross-sectional state proportions alone cannot identify rates or directions of conversion.
question: Which cannot be inferred from one cross-sectional atlas alone?
options: The exact transition rate between two states
Relative frequencies of measured states
Presence of state-associated markers

reference.label: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory, Nature (2026)

decisionRule: A UMAP or cross-sectional pseudotime orders expression profiles; actual direction and rate require lineage information, experimental perturbation or longitudinal observations.

title: Cell-state plasticity
takeaway: GBM malignant cells can show changes between transcriptional states under certain experimental contexts.
explanation: Xenograft systems have been used to study state switching.
caution: Population-level changes do not always constitute single-cell lineage tracing.
question: What does plasticity mean in this context?
options: Capacity of malignant cells to change transcriptional state
Permanent identity of every clone
A change in image contrast

reference.label: Neftel et al., Cell (2019), PMID 31327527

decisionRule: Distinguish reprogramming within a lineage from selection of pre-existing states using genetic barcodes, clone-aware sampling or lineage-linked repeated measurements.

title: State composition differs between tumors
takeaway: The relative abundance of malignant transcriptional programs can vary across tumors.
explanation: Two GBM patients can share state classes but with different proportions.
caution: Different proportions do not prove that tumors have wholly different mechanisms or prognoses.
question: What is a between-tumor state-composition difference?
options: One tumor contains more of a measured state than another
Differences between two regions of the same patient's tumor only
Differences between cells caused by dissociation-induced stress only

reference.label: Neftel et al., Cell (2019), PMID 31327527

decisionRule: Count independent patients, not cells. Compare state proportions per tumor with patient-aware uncertainty; different samples do not prove universal subtype rules.

title: Spatially ordered GBM state trajectory
takeaway: A 2026 atlas reported spatial and population-level evidence supporting a trajectory from developmental-like toward gliosis and hypoxia-associated programs.
explanation: Developmental-like states tended toward infiltrated regions; gliosis and hypoxia states occupied regions closer to necrosis.
caution: The paper's authors explicitly note no single-cell-resolution lineage tracing in the organoid model; do not treat the arrow as universal destiny.
question: How should the dev-like → gliosis → hypoxia arrow be interpreted?
options: An evidence-supported, context-dependent population trajectory
A proven irreversible fate for every malignant cell
A timeline recorded from each sampled cell

reference.label: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory, Nature (2026)

decisionRule: Map histological region and malignant program together. Co-localized gliosis/hypoxia and dev-like states support a spatial pattern but not a tracked path for each individual cell.

title: MES-like and injury-response programs overlap
takeaway: Some previously labeled MES-like glioblastoma expression patterns overlap with glial injury-response and hypoxia-associated programs.
explanation: The 2026 atlas reinterprets certain mesenchymal-associated malignant states as gliosis/hypoxia responses.
caution: This does not establish that all mesenchymal biology in all cancers is identical to an injury response.
question: Why is 'MES-like = fibroblast' incorrect?
options: It is a transcriptional resemblance, not proof of transdifferentiation
MES-like cells must have undergone an irreversible lineage conversion
Expression of MES-associated genes is restricted to malignant cells

reference.label: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory, Nature (2026)

decisionRule: Measure stress/ECM programs such as VIM/CD44/CHI3L1 and verify malignant genetics. Reactive nonmalignant glia can express overlapping injury-response genes.

title: A recurrence percentage needs its cohort
takeaway: The saved note quotes 79% local/in-field first recurrences, but provides insufficient study and cohort details to verify that exact fraction.
explanation: Recurrence location estimates depend on radiotherapy field definitions, follow-up and case selection.
caution: Could not verify the exact 79% claim with a peer-reviewed primary source in this check.
question: What should you do before citing the 79% number?
options: Trace the original cohort and recurrence definition
Treat it as a universal biological constant
Use it as a patient-level prediction

reference.label: Stupp et al., NEJM (2005), PMID 15758009

decisionRule: Before quoting 79%, identify the paper, recurrence cohort, surgery/RT fields, and definition of 'local', 'in-field' or 'first' recurrence. Without those, do not use the percentage as established.

title: A claim of 'never used in tumors' is risky
takeaway: The saved note says Spatial NT-seq has never been applied to tumors; this absolute claim was not verified.
explanation: A negative literature claim requires a time-bounded and systematic search, with clearly defined assay.
caution: Do not teach 'never' or build novelty on this statement without verification.
question: How can you evaluate a 'first application' claim?
options: Perform a scoped, dated literature review across assay synonyms
Infer it from a single review abstract
Assume an unpublished dataset cannot exist

reference.label: La Manno et al., Nature (2018), PMID 30089906

decisionRule: An absolute 'first study' or 'never applied' claim requires a search dated to the claim with assay synonyms, tissue definitions, code/data registries and preprints; one paper cannot prove absence.

title: RNA velocity estimates local transcriptional dynamics
takeaway: Models use spliced and unspliced RNA abundance to infer local change of expression state under kinetic assumptions.
explanation: A velocity vector may suggest a likely direction in an expression manifold.
caution: It is an inference, not a direct observation of where the same cell will move or what it will become.
question: Does a velocity arrow directly track a cell in time?
options: No, it is model-based inference
A velocity vector is direct lineage tracing of the same cell across time
A modeled vector proves that the predicted endpoint must occur

reference.label: La Manno et al., Nature (2018), PMID 30089906

decisionRule: Velocity arrows follow a kinetic model fitted to spliced/unspliced abundances. Assess transcript capture, residuals, steady-state/dynamical assumptions and perturbation/lineage evidence.

title: Two timepoints do not reveal conversion mechanisms
takeaway: Shifts in cell-state proportions between two samples can arise from transitions, differential survival or proliferation.
explanation: A state becoming more abundant after treatment could reflect selective killing rather than conversion.
caution: Distinguishing mechanisms can require lineage, proliferation/death and genotype-anchored data.
question: Within one GBM, the MES-like fraction is 20% before therapy and 40% after therapy. Which conclusion is defensible without lineage information?
options: The measured fraction changed; switching versus selection is unresolved
20% of malignant cells necessarily converted into MES-like state
Every surviving MES-like cell arose only after treatment

reference.label: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory, Nature (2026)

decisionRule: Example: MES-like increases from 20% to 40% after therapy. This is consistent with switching, differential survival, proliferation or sampling; lineage tracing or matched clonal controls separate hypotheses.
optionFeedback: Correct: a proportion change can reflect cell-state transitions, differential survival, proliferation, sampling or mixtures.
Incorrect: the difference in proportions is not a fraction of cells proven to have switched.
Incorrect: pre-existing MES-like cells may preferentially survive or expand.

title: Expression-based CNV inference is indirect
takeaway: Transcriptomic patterns may suggest large-scale copy-number alterations, but scRNA-seq does not directly count DNA copies.
explanation: Chr7 gain and chr10 loss are frequent GBM-associated patterns that may support malignant-cell annotation.
caution: Hypoxia, cell state, expression noise and normal reference choice may confound inferred CNVs.
question: A scRNA-seq cluster shows broad chr7-high/chr10-low expression. What is the strongest evidence for tumor-specific DNA copy changes?
options: Matched DNA-level CNV profiling or validated FISH signal
High RNA-derived CNV score alone, regardless of cell state
A UMAP cluster separated from normal immune cells

reference.label: Neftel et al., Cell (2019), PMID 31327527

decisionRule: Chromosome 7 expression enrichment plus chromosome 10 depletion can suggest a malignant CNV profile, but DNA sequencing or FISH establishes copy number more directly.
optionFeedback: Correct: DNA-based assays measure genomic gains/losses rather than using expression as a surrogate.
Incorrect: RNA-derived regional expression patterns can be affected by state and technical effects.
Incorrect: embedding distance does not prove a specific genomic alteration.

title: Dexamethasone can confound tumor transcriptomes
takeaway: Glucocorticoids used for symptomatic brain edema can change immune, inflammatory and tumor-associated expression.
explanation: Two samples receiving different steroid exposure may exhibit expression differences unrelated to the treatment of interest.
caution: Not every GBM patient receives dexamethasone, and dose/timing matter.
question: Two matched recurrent GBM samples differ in immune-gene expression; one patient received high-dose dexamethasone around surgery. How should RT attribution be handled?
options: Treat steroid exposure as an alternative explanation and model/check dose and timing
Ignore steroid use because dexamethasone only removes extracellular water
Attribute all immune-expression differences to radiotherapy

reference.label: Stupp et al., NEJM (2005), PMID 15758009

decisionRule: Collect dexamethasone dose, timing and indication for each tissue sample; compare steroid-matched groups or include treatment covariates before attributing immune-state differences to another therapy.
optionFeedback: Correct: glucocorticoids regulate immune and transcriptional pathways; exposure timing and dose matter.
Incorrect: dexamethasone has direct receptor-mediated immunoregulatory effects.
Incorrect: without accounting for a strong co-exposure, RT-specific attribution is unsupported.

title: Temozolomide versus MGMT repair
takeaway: Temozolomide creates DNA alkylation lesions, while MGMT repairs some O6-guanine lesions.
explanation: MGMT promoter methylation is associated with benefit from temozolomide in relevant GBM cohorts.
caution: MGMT is not a repair system for every lesion, and methylation is a biomarker rather than direct protein activity.
question: What is the mechanistic relation?
options: TMZ produces DNA lesions; MGMT can remove a subset
MGMT creates the alkylation lesions
TMZ directly encodes MGMT RNA

reference.label: Hegi et al., NEJM (2005), PMID 15758010

decisionRule: Separate TMZ-induced O6-methylguanine and other lesions from MGMT-specific direct reversal. Promoter methylation is a biomarker, not a direct functional assay of every lesion.

title: Stupp regimen
takeaway: The established Stupp approach uses radiotherapy with concomitant temozolomide followed by adjuvant temozolomide after appropriate surgical management.
explanation: In the landmark trial, radiotherapy plus TMZ improved survival compared with radiotherapy alone.
caution: Treatment selection depends on patient, tumor and current guidelines; a 2005 regimen is not every patient's complete care plan.
question: Which is the conventional sequence?
options: Maximal safe surgery → RT plus TMZ → adjuvant TMZ
Maximal safe surgery → temozolomide alone → RT only at progression
RT plus temozolomide before any surgery → observation without adjuvant treatment

reference.label: Stupp et al., NEJM (2005), PMID 15758009

decisionRule: Separate antitumor RT/TMZ treatment from supportive dexamethasone. Confirm whether the clinical schedule includes concomitant and adjuvant TMZ rather than inferring it from the patient's diagnosis.

title: Oxygen gradients and necrosis: avoid a fixed map
takeaway: Hypoxia-related states often appear near necrotic GBM areas, but oxygen supply depends on vascular function, diffusion and consumption.
explanation: The 2026 atlas reports spatial segregation between infiltrated dev-like regions and gliosis/hypoxia-associated regions.
caution: The stored vessel→oxygen→necrosis cartoon is not a universal one-dimensional spatial order; distances alone do not directly measure oxygen.
question: A perinecrotic region is hypoxic, but a nearby stained vessel lies only 15 µm away. What is the best next interpretation?
options: Vessel proximity does not guarantee oxygen delivery; check perfusion and consumption
The hypoxia measurement must be wrong because distance is short
The staining proves the vessel delivers normal oxygen to every neighbor

reference.label: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory, Nature (2026)

decisionRule: Measure regional hypoxia (for example oxygen-sensitive probes or validated indicators), perfusion and vessel quality; 2D distance to a stained vessel is not an oxygen measurement.
optionFeedback: Correct: abnormal vascular function and demand can decouple 2D vessel distance from actual oxygen availability.
Incorrect: observing a nearby vessel does not falsify independently measured low oxygen.
Incorrect: endothelial staining does not assess perfusion or local oxygen transport.

title: Normal brain cell roles
takeaway: Neurons transmit signals, astrocytes contribute to neural homeostasis, oligodendrocytes make CNS myelin and microglia are resident CNS immune cells.
explanation: These cell categories contribute differently to the brain tumor environment.
caution: Each cell type has multiple functions and states; no one-word label is exhaustive.
question: Which cell type primarily produces CNS myelin?
options: Oligodendrocytes
Microglia
T lymphocytes

reference.label: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory, Nature (2026)

decisionRule: Neuron: neuronal differentiation/synapse markers; oligodendrocyte: myelin markers; microglia: resident-myeloid programs; astrocyte: glial programs. Malignant cells can partially mimic each program.

title: Malignant and nonmalignant cells share a GBM section
takeaway: A GBM sample can contain tumor cells together with immune, vascular and normal neural/glial cells.
explanation: Cell-type composition changes spatially, influencing bulk and spatial gene profiles.
caution: A mixed expression profile is not equivalent to a malignant-cell-specific expression profile.
question: Why can bulk EGFR RNA be difficult to assign to one cell class?
options: Bulk RNA pools transcripts from many cell types
High EGFR RNA identifies the exact malignant cell of origin in bulk data
Any tumor-enriched transcript must originate only from malignant cells

reference.label: Neftel et al., Cell (2019), PMID 31327527

decisionRule: A bulk or spatial spot signal may reflect malignant, immune and normal cells. Use cell-resolved transcriptomics plus genomic identity or reliable deconvolution before attributing it to tumor cells.

title: NPC-, OPC-, AC- and MES-like are resemblance labels
takeaway: Common malignant programs resemble neural progenitor, oligodendrocyte precursor, astrocytic or mesenchymal-associated transcription.
explanation: Gene signatures help annotate malignant state identities.
caution: States may overlap, and marker-based calls require malignant identity established separately.
question: What does AC-like assert?
options: An astrocyte-associated expression program in a malignant cell
The cell is a normal astrocyte
A measurement of absolute oxygen

reference.label: Neftel et al., Cell (2019), PMID 31327527

decisionRule: Classify malignant cells by independent genetic evidence, then score NPC/OPC/AC/MES programs; similarity to a normal cell type is not proof of that lineage.

title: MES-like is not exclusively malignant
takeaway: Some injury-associated gene programs can be shared between malignant cells and reactive nonmalignant glia.
explanation: A nonmalignant astrocyte and a malignant cell may express overlapping stress-related genes.
caution: Shared genes do not prove the two cell types are biologically identical.
question: An astrocyte-like cell near necrosis expresses CD44, VIM and a hypoxia program. Is that sufficient to label it malignant GBM?
options: No; confirm malignant genotype or other independent cancer-cell identity evidence
Yes; CD44 and VIM are cancer-specific markers
Yes; all cells adjacent to necrosis are malignant

reference.label: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory, Nature (2026)

decisionRule: VIM/CD44/CHI3L1 or hypoxia/stress genes can be expressed in reactive glia. Use orthogonal malignant identity, such as DNA copy-number alterations, before labeling a cell as malignant.
optionFeedback: Correct: reactive nonmalignant glia can share stress and injury-response genes with GBM programs.
Incorrect: CD44/VIM and hypoxia-associated genes are not exclusive to malignant cells.
Incorrect: regions around necrosis can contain nonmalignant immune, vascular and glial cells.

title: Therapy-associated MES enrichment is not proof of switching
takeaway: MES-like or injury-response states can be more prevalent in treated or recurrent tumors in some studies.
explanation: Pre/post samples may show different state composition.
caution: Selection, region sampling and inflammation can also explain a difference; the highlight did not specify one causally decisive cohort.
question: What cannot a pre/post MES-like increase prove by itself?
options: That every cell switched into MES-like state
That measured frequencies differ
That a state-associated marker changed

reference.label: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory, Nature (2026)

decisionRule: Pre/post MES-like enrichment is a difference in composition, not per-cell reprogramming. Compare clone-aware longitudinal data, proliferation and survival signals to test competing mechanisms.

title: Genetic drivers modulate state frequencies
takeaway: GBM amplifications such as EGFR, PDGFRA or CDK4 can associate with different malignant expression programs.
explanation: State composition reflects a mixture of genotype and cell-context effects.
caution: These are associations, not one-to-one genotype→cell-state labels.
question: What is accurate about PDGFRA amplification?
options: It can bias state abundance but does not define every cell's state
It guarantees all cells become OPCs
It identifies immune microglia

reference.label: Neftel et al., Cell (2019), PMID 31327527

decisionRule: Check EGFR, PDGFRA and CDK4 alteration status against graded state scores within patients and clones; genotype-to-state relations are tendencies rather than categorical labels.

title: IDH mutation and 2-hydroxyglutarate
takeaway: Specific cancer-associated IDH1/IDH2 mutations confer neomorphic enzymatic activity that produces D-2-hydroxyglutarate.
explanation: A glioma with an appropriate IDH mutation can accumulate 2-HG.
caution: Not every IDH variant is oncogenic or has the same enzymatic effect; mutation class matters.
question: What is the distinctive effect of common glioma-associated IDH1 mutations?
options: Gain of an abnormal reaction producing 2-HG
Loss of all cellular enzymes
Guaranteed amplification of EGFR

reference.label: Dang et al., Nature (2009), PMID 19935646

decisionRule: Check the exact IDH1/IDH2 variant and D-2-hydroxyglutarate evidence: canonical glioma-associated neomorphic substitutions differ from benign or loss-of-function IDH variation.

title: EGFRvIII: a deletion-derived receptor variant
takeaway: EGFRvIII is an EGFR deletion variant associated with ligand-independent signaling in some GBM tumors.
explanation: A mutant receptor lacking part of the extracellular ligand-binding domain may signal abnormally.
caution: The exact exon-numbering details should be confirmed against a reference transcript; do not assume every tumor carries EGFRvIII.
question: Which statement is defensible?
options: EGFRvIII is a variant receptor, not a synonym for EGFR amplification
EGFR amplification inevitably produces the vIII deletion
EGFRvIII and EGFR amplification cannot occur in the same tumor

reference.label: EGFRvIII references — further verification recommended

decisionRule: Distinguish EGFR gene amplification (copy-number gain) from EGFRvIII deletion-derived transcript/protein. They can coexist but neither implies the other in every tumor.

title: GBM atlas: 12 tumors and 97 Visium sections
takeaway: The 2026 Nature spatial GBM study profiled 12 human tumors, using 97 Visium sections for spatial comparisons.
explanation: The authors also employed orthogonal modalities and analyzed recurring tissue microenvironments.
caution: 97 is a number of sections, not patients; individual tumors contributed more than one section.
question: In this atlas, what does 'n = 97' mean?
options: Visium sections, not 97 independent patients
97 single cells
97 protein markers

reference.label: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory, Nature (2026)

decisionRule: Use 12 as the independent tumor count when analyzing patient-level replication; 97 sections are repeated spatial samples nested within those tumors.
